The must-sees

9 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Church · 1852

    Helsinki Cathedral

    Designed by Carl Ludvig Engel, it was finished in 1852, twelve years after his death. It was first named St. Nicholas’ Church after the Russian tsar Nicholas I.

    Look for

    Inside, the plain white church holds statues of Martin Luther, Philipp Melanchthon and Mikael Agricola, who brought the Reformation to Finland.

  2. 02
    Station · 1919

    Helsinki Central Station

    Designed by Eliel Saarinen, it was completed in 1919. The lantern holders by the entrance are among the best-known faces of Helsinki.

  3. 03
    Market

    Market Square

    Stalls sell berries, fish and handicrafts much of the year. Boats to Suomenlinna leave from its quay.

    Look for

    Find the granite obelisk with a double-headed eagle: the Empress’s Stone, from 1835, the oldest public monument in Helsinki.

  4. 04
    Culture · 2018

    Oodi Central Library

    It opened in December 2018 as a project marking a century of Finnish independence. Visitors can borrow books, sew, 3D-print or simply sit on the top-floor terrace.

    Look for

    On the top floor, the white ceiling ripples over one open hall of books, known as Book Heaven.

  5. 05
    Square

    Senate Square

    Carl Ludvig Engel designed the square after Helsinki became the capital in 1812. The statue of Tsar Alexander II at its centre dates from 1894.

    Look for

    Around the base of the tsar’s statue, four figures stand for Law, Peace, Light and Labour.

  6. 06
    Landmark · 1967

    Sibelius Monument

    Eila Hiltunen’s monument to Jean Sibelius was unveiled in 1967. The face was added after debate over the abstract design.

    Look for

    Step underneath the pipes and look up through them at the sky.

  7. 07
    Fortress

    Suomenlinna

    Sweden began building it in 1748, when Finland was part of the Swedish realm, under Augustin Ehrensvärd. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to about 800 residents.

    Look for

    In the main courtyard of the fortress, find the tomb of Augustin Ehrensvärd, buried in the stronghold he built.

  8. 08
    Church · 1969

    Temppeliaukio Church

    Designed by the brothers Timo and Tuomo Suomalainen, it was completed in 1969. The bare rock walls give it acoustics that draw concerts as well as services.

    Look for

    Look up: the dome is a coil of copper strip, resting on a ring of skylights cut between it and the rock.

  9. 09
    Church · 1868

    Uspenski Cathedral

    Completed in 1868, it is often called the largest Orthodox church in Western Europe. Its bricks came from the Bomarsund fortress in Åland, destroyed in the Crimean War.

    Look for

    Inside, look for the gilded iconostasis, the screen of icons before the altar.
